summary: Eight distinct antiprotozoal/anthelmintic lab-assay records for isolated eugenol or separately tested clove oil, plus NIH toxicity caveat. Experimental IC50/EC50 values are never human dose suggestions.

The antileishmanial activity of eugenol associated with lipid storage reduction rather than membrane properties alterations

bioactivities.observed_effect: Eugenol inhibited trophozoite growth and adherence in culture.
bioactivities.mechanism: Altered morphology, adherence and organelles were observed, without validating a unique binding target.
bioactivities.dose_translation: Laboratory assay exposure only. No safe or effective human or livestock treatment dose established.
bioactivities.limitations: No human giardiasis treatment trial established by this study.

bioactivities.observed_effect: Clove oil mixture inhibited growth and adherence, but this is not the same as purified eugenol.
bioactivities.mechanism: Cellular structural damage observed in vitro.
bioactivities.dose_translation: Laboratory assay exposure only. No safe or effective human or livestock treatment dose established.
bioactivities.limitations: Essential oil is not clove buds or clove tea and cannot be taken as a proven antiparasitic medicine.

bioactivities.study_model: promastigote cell culture and laboratory lipid assays
bioactivities.observed_effect: In vitro parasite growth inhibition and decreased lipid droplet content.
bioactivities.mechanism: Decreased lipid stores may be associated with the effect; membrane effects arose at higher exposure than antiparasitic IC50.
bioactivities.dose_translation: Laboratory assay exposure only. No safe or effective human or livestock treatment dose established.
bioactivities.limitations: No proof of leishmaniasis cure in people; species and parasite stage matter.

bioactivities.observed_effect: Eugenol showed measurable in vitro promastigote activity.
bioactivities.mechanism: Docking/immune hypotheses not demonstrated receptor binding.
bioactivities.dose_translation: Laboratory assay exposure only. No safe or effective human or livestock treatment dose established.
bioactivities.limitations: In vitro concentration does not translate to a human dose or generalize to other Leishmania.

bioactivities.observed_effect: Eugenol alone had activity in amastigote assays; drug-combination findings are separate.
bioactivities.dose_translation: Laboratory assay exposure only. No safe or effective human or livestock treatment dose established.
bioactivities.limitations: Not a human trial; host toxicity and achievable human exposures unknown.

bioactivities.observed_effect: Eugenol affected hatching of parasite eggs.
bioactivities.mechanism: Potential biochemical interactions were only modeled by docking.
bioactivities.dose_translation: Laboratory assay exposure only. No safe or effective human or livestock treatment dose established.
bioactivities.limitations: Veterinary gastrointestinal nematode; in vivo safety and effectiveness were not established.

bioactivities.mechanism: Precise molecular target not experimentally verified.
bioactivities.dose_translation: Laboratory assay exposure only. No safe or effective human or livestock treatment dose established.
bioactivities.limitations: Not demonstrated for treating animals or humans.

bioactivities.study_model: in vitro adult worm motility assay
bioactivities.observed_effect: Adult movement was inhibited; immobility does not necessarily equal worm death.
bioactivities.mechanism: Morphological damage observed and molecular docking was explored, not proof of direct binding.
bioactivities.dose_translation: Laboratory assay exposure only. No safe or effective human or livestock treatment dose established.
bioactivities.limitations: Adult worms in experimental cultures are not live-host clearance evidence.

safety.alert: NIH LiverTox reports severe liver and kidney injury and neurologic toxicity after clove/eugenol oil overdose, particularly in children. Experimental antiparasitic concentrations provide no safe intake regimen.
